SMTO-EXE-0264 — This workflow must run on a specific computer that isn't selected

GUID: 82f5d507-eb23-5cfa-ae37-adc6e6e43003
Slug: recipe-gateway-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • This workflow was saved to always run through one particular Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer. This run used a different Gateway or none, so SMTO stopped before any steps ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and check that the Gateway this workflow used before is listed and connected. The workflow can only run through that exact Gateway.
  2. If that computer was reinstalled, renamed or replaced, its Gateway may now be different. Select Save to workflow on your original message and enter the current Gateway under Execution settings › Gateway ID. This older workflow only runs through the exact Gateway it was saved with, so a new save is needed to change it.
  3. If the old workflow ran on a schedule, open Schedules and select Delete on that schedule, then use Schedule on the new workflow's card instead. The old schedule will keep stopping here because it still points to the old Gateway.

What success looks like

  • The workflow starts on the intended computer and its first steps appear in the run's conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name and the computer it should run on, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't point the old workflow at another computer just to get past this; its steps were set up for the original one.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A recorded workflow with a fixed target policy was started with a missing or different selected Gateway than its saved gateway_id.

What this means

  • A workflow with a fixed Gateway identity was invoked with a different or missing selected Gateway. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • A workflow with a fixed Gateway identity was invoked with a different or missing selected Gateway.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the workflow target_policy.gateway_id with the invocation's selected Gateway; this check alone does not test network health.

How to fix it

  • Compare workflow.target_policy.gateway_id with the invocation's gateway_id or gateway_selection.primary_gateway_id (validation.revalidate). Start the workflow with the fixed Gateway once it passes normal availability checks, or deliberately save a new workflow with the intended target.
  • Select the workflow's fixed Gateway, or deliberately review and save a new target policy before new work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The invocation selects the exact fixed Gateway and its ordinary availability checks pass.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
